observation: Two 38-row runs produced identical normalized decisions; critical mutations remained full while presentation moved from full toward reduced, deferred, and dropped as pressure rose.
interpretation: A small explicit runtime-envelope contract can separate fidelity, criticality, and transport without Unity or a generic IL scheduler.
assumption_changed: The first gate requires live frame timing before its decision and evidence shape can be evaluated.
decision: Keep the policy and receipt; replace synthetic cost units with CRE-0 measurements before selecting a live call site.

observation: WebSocket fallback and bound UDP each delivered the same nine selected presentation work IDs with sequence 1 through 9; all 23 deferred or dropped decisions remained absent from transport.
interpretation: The runtime-envelope decision can drive the production Gateway motion seam and prove negative carriage by work identity rather than aggregate counts.
assumption_changed: A real Unity client is required to verify that gate suppression reaches the intended Gateway transport boundary.
decision: Retain the policy-to-route seam; test duplicate, reorder, bounded loss, and reconnect separately, while keeping critical-state carriage outside this claim.

observation: All bounded sequence, gap, wrap, resume, and detached-token predictions passed, but ten accepted source frames produced eighteen aggregate relay deliveries; UDP also counted its endpoint-bind setup frame.
interpretation: The one-input/one-relay prediction confused source acceptance with per-recipient delivery and mixed setup traffic into the measurement window.
assumption_changed: Accepted source frames equal aggregate relay deliveries and raw receive counters begin at gameplay zero.
decision: Retain the refuted receipts; baseline after setup and measure source acceptance, one observer, and regional fanout separately without changing Gateway behavior.

observation: Both Gateway drivers accepted ten source frames, delivered ten to the primary observer, produced eighteen aggregate topology-derived relay deliveries, and rejected three stale frames; UDP rejected the detached token.
interpretation: Motion freshness behavior is consistent across UDP and WebSocket fallback for the bounded cases, while delivery cost scales with eligible recipient fanout.
assumption_changed: Runtime-envelope pressure can be modeled from local patch cost and source event count alone.
decision: Keep the freshness guard and make future cost models fanout-aware; do not infer critical-state reliability or Unity feel.

observation: Two 60-row runs matched: direct/latest/expiry applied 19/14/12 samples, coalesced 0/5/5, expired 0/0/2, and preserved final source sequences 13 and 9; expiry capped applied age at 75 ms.
interpretation: Latest-wins and expiry can bound presentation apply work without final-state regression in the synthetic vector, but savings and fidelity risk depend on whether the seam is client-side, per-recipient, or pre-fanout.
assumption_changed: A single coalescer placement reduces client, Gateway, and network cost equally.
decision: Retain the policy primitive; replay captured timing before choosing an opt-in placement, and keep critical mutations outside it.

observation: Two 12-row model runs matched: the checked-in 20 Hz receive path already coalesces latest per ZDO, while render apply requests FPS x fresh-remotes calls; at 60 FPS this is three applies per accepted snapshot and 6,000 calls/s for 100 modeled remotes.
interpretation: The next cost seam is not another latest-wins receive cache. Object binding, per-frame interpolation, and possible native transform competition need separate measurement before changing cadence or smoothing.
assumption_changed: The current client applies each accepted motion snapshot once or uses velocity extrapolation.
decision: Keep current chase-latest as rollback; add bounded phase rollups, then compare captured timing against a two-snapshot timeline without changing critical-state or live authority.

observation: Cumulative receive, drain/coalesce, bind, LateUpdate, error, freshness, and source-agnostic interframe-displacement rollups now flow through the existing client JSONL contract; a three-row fixture produced the predicted 40 received samples, 3 applies per received sample, 20 us mean bind, and conservative lifetime-max labels.
interpretation: The existing Companion capture is sufficient for bounded phase evidence; no per-frame logger or new observer service is required. The two-client feel harness can collect and analyze both clients with one switch.
assumption_changed: Phase measurement requires a new telemetry service or human-managed file collection.
decision: Ship the observation-only counters and run one straight role-reversal capture before changing interpolation, binding, stale retention, or authority.

observation: The disposable lab accepted and SHA-256 verified the exact clean 4120497 DLL while Docker, Compose, the local Valheim server, and MCP Gateway were healthy; the stop gate found no seeded Valheim install or existing character profile in the client volume, so no client container was started.
interpretation: Autonomous lifecycle and exact-artifact delivery are ready, but the current local headless lane needs a one-time licensed Steam install/profile seed before it can replace a physical-client window.
assumption_changed: The retained disposable client volumes still contain the previously seeded Valheim install and character.
decision: Keep the stop gate; never fall back to the dirty worktree bin. Use the m31-aligned physical clients for the next bounded run or seed the disposable Steam profile in a dedicated operator window.

observation: The first Wave 0 audit rejected the healthy m31 package pointer because it incorrectly required package.release to equal package.mod_release. After separating package identity from admitted mod identity, the audit passed P7, OMEN, i5, package-hash, profile/config, heartbeat-age, and motion-endpoint checks.
interpretation: Rapid client-pull packages are compatible with a frozen Gateway when their baked mod identity remains admitted; readiness must compare both identities and the package hash rather than collapse them into one release label.
assumption_changed: The public package pointer ID must equal the Gateway/admitted mod release ID.
decision: Keep Gateway and server on m30, retain m31 as the client package pointer, and proceed to one bounded joined-client role reversal.
